messages.author: bc11fbb928eb77ff
messages.subject: problem of code in Nimble?
parts:
Hi all,

I am encountering a problem when I use Nimble functions called with nimble:: and without using library(nimble) or require(nimble) - which is required to use Nimble functions inside a package function. This problem disappears when I load Nimble with librray(nimble). Here is the problem with a reproducible example:

set.seed(1)
y1000<-rnorm(n=1000,mean=600,sd=30)


  ModelData <-list(mass = y1000)
  ModelConsts <- list(nobs = length(y1000))
 
  modelCode<-nimble::nimbleCode(
  {
   
    # Priors
    population.mean ~ dunif(0,5000)
    population.sd ~ dunif(0,100)
   
    # Precision = 1/variance
    population.variance <- population.sd * population.sd
   
    # Normal parameterized by precision
    precision <- 1 / population.variance
 
    # Likelihood
    for(i in 1:nobs){
      mass[i] ~ dnorm(population.mean, precision)
    }
  })
 
 
Model <- nimble::nimbleModel(code = modelCode, name = 'Nimble', constants = ModelConsts,  data = ModelData)

I then get an error telling me that it is impossible to find the "getNimbleOption" function. When ding a traceback() I get the info that this problem arises inside the function init_isDataEnv(). When I do librray(nimble) first, there is no problem.

Looking at the code (e.g. https://rdrr.io/cran/nimble/src/R/BUGS_model.R) I was wondering if getNimbleOption shuld not be replaced throughout by nimble::getNimbleOption.

Am I correct?

The problem appears both with R4.3.0 & R.4.1.2 under Windows (versions of nimble: nimble_0.13.1in both).

Thanks very much in advance.

All the best,

Frédéric Gosselin

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: problem of code in Nimble?
parts:
Hi Frédéric,

We've often had packages that use NIMBLE have nimble in `Depends` in their DESCRIPTION, or possibly in `Imports`, with `import(nimble)` in NAMESPACE.

If instead you want to use `importFrom` in NAMESPACE, which is probably when the issue would arise, I'll have to look into the scoping questions. I want to do this because it should be possible to do what you want, but I probably wouldn't get to it for a bit and not sure it would be able to be fixed for the next release.

-chris

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: problem of code in Nimble?
parts:
Hi Frédéric,

Sorry about the delay in following up here. Unfortunately, I don't think changing how we refer to functions from the nimble package inside of methods such as `init_isDataEnv` will fully solve the problem (I can provide the gory details if you wish, though there are some comments in this GitHub issue). Instead, the approach we and others have taken in having packages that rely on `nimble` is to include `nimble` in `Depends` in the `DESCRIPTION` file rather than in `Imports` so that `nimble` is attached when the nimble-relying package is loaded, and therefore all objects in the nimble namespace can be found at the user level. CRAN doesn't encourage this, but it is allowed. 

-chris
